reply:
Here is the same answer with context.

**Where this fits.** You asked how the task continues after you approve it. The task runs as a Graph. The Graph has Nodes and paths. A Node is one step. A Checkpoint is a saved record of the Graph state that can help it continue.

**What happens at your approval.**
1. The Graph stops at the confirmation boundary. It does not continue until you approve.
2. At that point the task saves a Checkpoint. This Checkpoint ties your reply to the execution that is suspended.
3. After the Graph starts again (re-entry), the next Node makes the report.

**The limit.** The Checkpoint does not guarantee that an external file write happens only once. If a crash occurs, the external file write can occur more than one time. This answer gives no exactly-once guarantee for that write.

Note: the repository has only `GLOSSARY.md`, so I used that file. It has no `GLOSSARY-MAP.md`.

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Graph | A set of Nodes and paths that controls a task. |
| Node | One step in the Graph. |
| Checkpoint | A saved record of the Graph state that can help it continue. |

Use these names when explaining this task. A Checkpoint does not guarantee that an external action happens only once.
